How are you testing performance? Are you launching the app and immediately reading FPS, or are you giving the shader cache time to warm up? 

Keep in mind that for the first minute or so Godot will compile optimized shaders in the background which means that your game will be running with the un-optimized Uber shader. 

To get an accurate performance measurement, you need to let the game run for 30 seconds or so (the exact amount of time depends on how many shaders you use). 

For more information see https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/performance/pipeline_compilations.html

That is important because [#104194](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/104194) was bisected to the introduction of 2D batching. 2D batching will have no impact on the MRP in this issue and was introduced in dev3.

Try enabling `input_devices/buffering/agile_event_flushing` project setting. It is related to inputs in the render thread. PRs for details https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/93933 and https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/94052.

Likely candidate for the regression https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/94799 since it touches the input flushing system between 4.4.dev3 and 4.4.dev4.

I looked into this a bit myself. With a device with an Immortalis-G715s GPU, I couldn't reproduce a performance difference. 

But with a device with an Adreno 640, I could. However, notably, once I enabled the sky background, the performance difference disappeared. 

I couldn't reproduce a difference in performance related to touch input. However, I suspect that it has to do with the introduction of Swappy https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/96439. Swappy will intentionally reduce FPS in order to minimize input latency when it detects that it is safe to do so. I suspect that somehow Swappy is wrongly trying to reduce input latency and frame rate is suffering as a result. 

So I think there are two issues here and both are likely dependent on the device being tested. 

The issue that I was able to reproduce seems to be connected to how we manage subpasses. When using subpasses, you take away the Vulkan driver's ability to do certain optimizations, but using subpasses itself is an optimization! Basically, using subpasses is faster if you are writing to most pixels multiple times (once in the opaque pass, once for sky, once for transparent, once for tonemapping). But if you are only writing during the opaque pass and the tonemap pass, and especially if you are leaving huge chunks of the screen empty, it can be faster to not use subpasses since the driver can decide to skip entire tiles that won't be rendered to. 

I suspect that most of the performance difference that I was able to reproduce can be fixed by falling back to our non-subpass path when there is no sky or transparent pass present

@brcontainer What does the regular profiler say on your device (the non-"visual" profiler)?

Looking at the rendering timings are not helpful in this case since they are so low. The difference between 0.08ms and 0.68 ms is 12500 FPS to 1470 FPS. Since your device is locked to 45 FPS, we can be reasonably sure that difference in frame time doesn't account for it. 

Similarly, the difference between 60 FPS and 45 FPS is 16.666 -> 22.2222 = 5.555555. You need to be looking out for something that causes a decrease by 5.55555 ms _or more_. 

Further, I tested on a weaker device than yours and was locked to 60 FPS in both cases. So it is quite clear the problem is more than just performance getting worse. Something is going wrong and causing your device to lock to 45 FPS. 

This is why I strongly suspect the issue is related to swappy/input. There are a number of things you could try that have been suggested above:
1. perform multiple swipes on android screen (lifting the finger off the screen each time) ([suggested here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/109251#issuecomment-3268742645))
2. Try enabling `input_devices/buffering/agile_event_flushing` project setting ([suggested here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/109251#issuecomment-3270300525))
3. Try different Swappy modes here: [`display/window/frame_pacing/android/swappy_mode`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_projectsettings.html#class-projectsettings-property-display-window-frame-pacing-android-swappy-mode)

I even have 3 Render Canvas entries. However, this is due to the fact that I actually loaded 3 canvas layers at the same time. That's definitely one more thing I wanted to adjust ;-) But maybe that's also the problem with the thread creator. Unfortunately I can't test at the moment whether it was already displayed like this in 4.4.

3. Try different Swappy modes here: [`display/window/frame_pacing/android/swappy_mode`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_projectsettings.html#class-projectsettings-property-display-window-frame-pacing-android-swappy-mode)

Thinking about this some more I am almost certain this is a consequence of enabling swappy. It seems like the OPs device has a 90hz screen. Swappy will force using a multiple of the screen refresh rate in order to provide a stable frame time with vsync. 

Therefore, if the game isn't able to manage 90 FPS consistently, swappy will lock the game to 45. The fact that the game was running at 60 before tells us that it wasn't able to reach 90, so it makes sense that swappy is lowering it to 45

Whether relevant or not, after updating Android to version 15, the issue no longer occurred. I tried all the suggested steps to reproduce it, but without success — which is why my response was delayed.

I also tried for a long time to get a device with older software to provide clear feedback on the issue, but that's not something I can currently do.

A likely relevant detail is that using `pipeline_forced_on` and `auto_fps_pipeline_forced_on` will lock the frame rate to 30fps (exactly as described in the [documentation](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_projectsettings.html#class-projectsettings-property-display-window-frame-pacing-android-swappy-mode), considering **_my device has 60Hz_**).

 Therefore, _I can't confirm that the issue is related to the pipeline_ (and from all the tests I did I believe they are not related), as the situation at the time was a variation between 45fps and 47fps (and sometimes even reaching 52fps for a few moments), even after 10 minutes of playtime.

At the time, he also performed several swipes on the screen, but there was no variation in the fps, and even testing today, it doesn't reproduce the issue with swipes.

*Note:* I speculate that it could be a conflict with something related to the older version of "One UI" (Samsung), but it's just speculation.

To clarify, both MRP and my other 3D projects (4 projects) that I used as parameters are working fine using Godot 4.5 for Android, so it seems the issue has been resolved (or is no longer reproducible). I really appreciate everyone’s effort and input. From my side, this issue can be closed.
